correctness.rationale: The star Krylov matrix has leaf entries forming a triangular polynomial basis, giving exactly prod(w_i)^2 prod(diff)^2. Cayley–Hamilton factorization through a companion basis makes the normalized Gramian determinant jointly analytic uniformly on the closed simplex, allowing global rather than merely interior control. Exponential-alternant Schur coefficients and three independent Jacobi-ensemble trace moments yield the universal log-T^2 term n tr(A^2)/(2(4n^2-1)); the exact rational checker reproduced the first three coefficients in eight independent diagonal examples. For the star, tr(A)=-2B and tr(A^2)=B^2+3sum(w_i^2). Laguerre equilibrium, strict Hessian negativity and two explicitly reconstructed Hessian-vector relations then prove the constrained T^2 displacement and global uniqueness for sufficiently small T. All quantifiers, star size and budget assumptions, zero-weight and collision boundaries, and O(T^3) limits are explicit; enumeration is not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Existing work supplies star Vandermonde controllability, the Laguerre leading optimum, related fixed-step discrete Gramian design, general edge weight controllability optimization, and the generic determinant first-order trace correction. The assessed new conclusion is the explicit nonzero continuous-time finite-horizon T² drift of every optimal star spoke, proved globally unique for sufficiently small horizons. No exact implication from the closest inspected sources or recoverable historical claims provides this shift; unindexed equivalent perturbation formulas remain possible.
residual_risks: A general determinant expansion beyond first order or a network-specific horizon optimization may be recorded in literature absent from indexed searches.

The classical Schur/Jacobi identities used in the proof are not new and may make the universal trace coefficient implicit in other general sources; only the explicit combined finite-horizon design conclusion is claimed.

value.rationale: The objective is exactly squared unit-energy reachable-ellipsoid volume, a natural D-optimal controllability criterion. The nonzero second-order drift gives a concrete, edge-by-edge finite-horizon correction to a known leading design, distinguishes continuous-time finite horizons from the fixed-step discrete solution, and provides global uniqueness up to symmetry rather than a local heuristic. The effect is physically motivated by differing finite-time reachability of differently weighted spokes, not an arbitrary slice or an unmotivated numerical constant.
